game.name: Heroes of Hammerwatch

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Heroes of Hammerwatch is a chill top-down action dungeon-crawler roguelite. PepperHead has only tried it two or three times because the trailers look exciting but reaching the bosses requires a slow grind. He finds the early game repetitive and not very engaging, though the game is cute and he may return someday. He places it in a low B tier for now.
praise: Looks cool and cute in trailers
Promise of lots of content and cool stuff deeper in
He could see himself coming back to it one day
criticism: Need to grind quite a bit to get started
Early game is boring and very repetitive
Always starts in the same dungeon with the same critters
Moment-to-moment gameplay not very engaging early on
Getting to the bosses takes a long time; pacing too slow
unique_points: Not very unique as a game; mostly notable for its appealing look
Needs upfront build-up and unlocking before the fun content is reachable
commentary.quote: it's cute though and I could see myself coming back to it one day
design_criteria: Early-game pacing: slow, grind-heavy start hurts it
Repetition: same starting dungeon and enemies every run
Meta-progression: requires building up before the game opens
Engagement of core gameplay: weak early on
Run length/time to bosses: long before reaching bosses

community.one_liner: A pixel-art, top-down action roguelite from Crackshell (published by Team17) where you push through procedurally generated dungeon floors solo or in 4-player online co-op, sending gold and ore back to a persistent town to upgrade seven (nine with DLC) heroes.
community.consensus_summary: Players rate it Very Positive on Steam (about 87-88% positive, roughly 9.5k reviews in the local data; the store page shows about 4.7k English reviews, with the last 30 days sitting at Mostly Positive, 75% of 20 reviews). Metacritic has no critic reviews, and its 14 user ratings average 7.2, which is less enthusiastic than Steam. The core combat, class variety and co-op are widely liked, but the most common complaint is that the meta-progression is slow and padded, which Steam reviewers describe as grindy well beyond the norm for a roguelite. It is a finished, content-rich game with three DLC expansions (Witch Hunter, Pyramid of Prophecy, Moon Temple) and a Workshop/level editor. Reviewers still report old bugs as of late 2025, including a character-overwrite save bug and black-screen issues, so polish is uneven. Its successor Heroes of Hammerwatch II now exists, so this entry is in maintenance territory. I could not retrieve critic reviews from major outlets, so critic sentiment is essentially absent.
best_things: Moment-to-moment top-down hack-and-slash/shoot combat is praised as good fun, even by reviewers who quit over grind
Persistent town with shopkeepers and upgrades gives a satisfying early progression loop; town unlocks carry across all heroes
Strong co-op: up to 4 players online, and several reviewers say it is far better with friends than solo
Seven distinct classes (nine with DLC) with different skill sets, plus item sets that scale builds as you collect pieces
Simple item model: no equipment management, pickups apply instantly, which keeps runs quick and easy to jump into
Risk/reward gold banking: you must send gold to town (with a random tax rate) or lose it if you die, which creates tension
Huge content volume: lots of floors, secrets, traps, bosses, New Game+ tiers and three expansions
Steam Workshop and a built-in level editor extend the game; mods are popular for speeding up or unlocking content
worst_things: Grind is the dominant complaint: maxing one character reportedly takes hundreds of thousands of gold while a run earns about 10-20k before tax
The gold tax mechanic (more gold held means a worse rate) is called pointless padding that slows progression
Upgrades and town purchases are per-character in many cases, so each new hero means re-buying expensive upgrades
Most traps and some enemy attacks have no invincibility frames, so players can be chain-hit and killed instantly
Chest/key system feels random: players report holding keys with no chests, or finding locked chests with no keys, and needing 40+ of a material that does not drop
Build diversity is shallow; many items are flat damage or speed boosts, and late runs feel like stacking bigger numbers
Reused assets and enemies from the first Hammerwatch make it feel less fresh to returning fans

Long-standing bugs: a reported save bug that deletes a character and replaces it with a copy of the last played one, random crashes, black screens on exit or at the final boss, and lobby disconnects in co-op
improvements: Share more upgrades (potions, blessings, stat upgrades) across all heroes instead of per character
Reduce or remove the gold tax, and lower prices of items like pets (one reviewer says 25k for a pet is too much)
Fix the character-deletion save bug and black-screen/crash issues that players say have persisted for years
Give more build variety and less flat-number item design so New Game+ runs feel different
Raise or remove shopkeeper purchase limits in dungeons and make key/chest and material drops less random
Add crossplay and improve multiplayer stability and desync handling; also better controller and Steam Deck support
unique_things: Town-building meta progression shared across a roster of heroes, rather than a single run-based unlock tree
Gold banking with random tax: send money home to keep it, or carry it at risk of losing everything on death
Item-set system with instant-apply pickups and no inventory or gear slots
Shortcut/skip mechanics and alternate paths through tiers, plus a huge New Game+ ladder (achievement hunters cite NG+7/NG+8 requirements)
Built-in level editor and Steam Workshop support, with popular mods adding classes and unlocks
Roguelite evolution of the original Hammerwatch's lose-it-all roguelike formula, set in the same universe
tedious_or_disliked: Repeating the same floors to farm the same two materials (gold and ore), with progress that feels slower the further you get
Needing to beat every boss with every character because those clears give permanent bonuses to all heroes, even classes you dislike
Progression slows after roughly NG+2 as runs become numbers-only scaling, per a 112-hour solo player who stopped at NG+4
Small corridors and heavy ranged enemy spam make individual fights annoying for some, especially solo
Death resets feel punishing because runs that die before banking resources yield nothing, which one Metacritic user called a hamster-wheel design
divisive_points: Co-op vs solo: reviewers repeatedly say it shines with friends but the grind is hard to justify alone
Grind tolerance: some players love the long town-and-character progression while others call it worse than mobile gacha games
Difficulty and build freedom: some find it easy and relaxed, others feel underpowered without gold spent on upgrades and find traps unfair
Workshop mods: several players say the game is only fun with progression-speed mods, which others see as a fix for design flaws
community.reception_notes: Released March 1, 2018 (Steam, Windows/Linux, no Mac) at $14.99, developed by Crackshell and published by Team17. The local Steam data shows a Very Positive all-time rating, and the recent window is slightly lower at Mostly Positive. Three paid expansions exist: Witch Hunter, Pyramid of Prophecy and Moon Temple. A sequel, Heroes of Hammerwatch II, exists and has its own DLC. Metacritic lists no critic reviews and only 14 user ratings (7.2), and I could not find an OpenCritic listing. I could not retrieve Reddit, news patch notes or outlet reviews because of tool limits, so launch-era critic reception and recent patch history are not verified here. The original Hammerwatch (2013) has a Metascore of 72 per Wikipedia, which is a different game. Late-2025/2026 Steam reviews still mention save-deletion, black-screen and disconnect bugs, suggesting low ongoing patch activity.
